what: oco-agent says what newly came into view
how: Every five minutes a user timer runs oco-say-what-is-new: it brings its own copy of what the observatory observed up to date (one git fetch, no API requests), and for the lenses of work and of problems asks ocoeco what is new in view since last time (ocoeco focus LENS --observed ... --since ...); each line is said to the author through oco-agent's voice. ocoeco says what is new and oco-agent carries it: neither knows the other.
why: The board pushed whole to the phone was the last thing lab-agent's daemon did for the author; what changed is what a person needs.
evidence: 2026-11-12, with OCO_SAY=echo: the first run said nothing and kept both lenses; an item taken out of the kept focus was the one thing said; run again at once, nothing was said; the timer is active.

what: Rotating the lab's GitHub token without it ever entering a repository
how: The lab makes a one-time RSA key pair in a private folder and prints only the public key. The new token is sealed with it (openssl pkeyutl, OAEP, SHA-256) and sent in a job; the lab opens it, checks its fingerprint and that it reaches the jobs repository, keeps the old aside for the way back, writes the new into ~/.config/lab-agent/token and env without printing either, destroys the key, restarts the voice, and asks oco-agent to restart between jobs. A later job proves the work runs and lands on it.
why: A job's text is kept in the jobs repository's history; a secret written there is written forever.
evidence: 2026-11-12: decrypted token matched the sealed one; 0 places still held the old; this landing went through the new token.

what: The lab observes what has run in every place it holds, and says what changed
how: Every quarter hour a user timer runs oco-observe-runs: ocoeco observe --root ~/Projects --only runs writes the latest finished run of each workflow on each place's default branch, and prints what changed since the last observation; a run that fails now is said to the author urgently through oco-agent's voice, one that passes again plainly. ocoeco observes and oco-agent speaks: neither knows the other.
why: On 2026-11-12, 111 runs had failed on main in three days and no one heard; GitHub's schedules are best-effort, the lab's own clock is not.
evidence: 2026-11-12: the first observation read 45 runs of 18 places for 46 requests; a run marked failing before was said to pass again, once - observed again at once, nothing was said; the timer is active.

how: A job goes to the lab machine, runs there, and its output returns.
why: The work must happen where the hardware is.

how: Each task is set, resumed and closed as it happens, and shown in the desktop's status bar.
why: The person sees what is being done without having to ask.

how: The person's messages are read at every pause, and each one is answered.
why: Being heard should not need interrupting.

how: Prints the ways of working, read live, to an agent before it works.
why: Good habits should arrive with the tool.

how: Jobs run in the background; progress goes to a notification channel and the status bar, never to a window that takes the keyboard.
why: A helper that interrupts the person it helps is not helping.
